title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to measure whether constrained prompting plus a deterministic generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) improves deterministic-verifier semantic correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents deterministically generated; model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; execution semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial sampled candidate reused across baseline and guarded conditions); at most one repair call permitted. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.0066667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; shared_initial_generation = 150; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We highlight the methodological lesson that preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the supplied execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

sections.introduction: Natural-language (NL) intent interfaces aim to let operators express desired network changes in free text that are automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work reports frequent LLM output errors—omissions, sequencing mistakes, and hallucinations—that can produce unsafe or unavailable network states if applied directly. A common mitigation is a generate→verify→repair pipeline in which an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants, and a repair step (automated or human) corrects violations before execution. We preregistered a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with a deterministic verifier-guided iterative repair materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) on N=150 deterministic synthetic intents. (2) Artifact-backed quantitative outcomes showing baseline_success_count = 149/150 and guarded_success_count = 150/150 under shared_initial_candidate semantics, with an absolute paired difference of ≈0.67 pp (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation—preregistered NetOps trials should include brief baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects—and concrete operational prescriptions for matching generation semantics, repair budgets, and power planning to deployment constraints.
sections.related_work: We position this study amid three strands relevant to NL→configuration translation and guarded agentic pipelines. First, empirical evaluations of intent-translation report modest semantic-correctness and emphasize prompt design, model competence, and oracle choice as dominant factors. Second, verifier-in-the-loop and generate→verify→repair systems (including verifier-guided fine-tuning and policy-guided reranking) generally reduce syntactic and semantic errors for infrastructure-as-code and configuration-repair tasks, although reported effect sizes vary with verifier expressiveness, repair budgets, and sampling semantics. Third, mature symbolic/network-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch and related engines) can serve as deterministic oracles for reachability/isolation and policy checks but have limited protocol and topology coverage, making verifier-coverage a key construct-validity concern. Security analyses further show that unguarded multi-tool agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions, motivating conservative gating and auditable verdicts. Our trial deliberately fixes three operational knobs emphasized by prior work: (a) the repair budget (one repair), (b) sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate), and (c) deterministic verifier as binary oracle—choices that bound the maximal observable marginal benefit of a guarded repair under our estimand.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 and frozen prior to any model outputs. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated via an exact two-sided McNemar test on deterministic-verifier pass/fail outcomes. Confirmatory sample: N=150 distinct synthetic intents generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across four intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like access, VLAN/MTU sequences, uplink switchover). Inclusion/exclusion rules (ambiguity detector, parser mapping checks, verifier-coverage checks), a one-retry rule for provider timeouts, and a preregistered power target (detect +15 percentage points at ≈80% power) were all archived and frozen. Execution semantics and adapter enforcement. A central design decision implemented in the runtime adapter was shared_initial_candidate: for each intent the adapter produced exactly one initial model generation and reused that identical sampled candidate when scoring both baseline and guarded conditions. The guarded pipeline was allowed at most one additional repair call only if the deterministic verifier failed that initial candidate. The adapter enforced these constraints and recorded provider accounting (artifact evidence: shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 1; model_calls_used = 151). Mapping preregistration labels to executed contrasts (required revision). The preregistration conceptually described three conditions A (baseline free-text), B (constrained template), and C (constrained + verifier feedback) and hypotheses H1/H2 correspondingly. Under the adapter-enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics the confirmed, executed, and archived primary contrast is C (guarded) versus A (baseline) using the identical initial sampled candidate per intent; B was not executed as an independent first-pass condition in this run and therefore no independent B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts are reported in the archived analysis. This manuscript reports outcomes for the actually executed paired contrast (C vs A under shared_initial_candidate) and adheres to the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor without post-lock analytic changes. Model, sampling, and deterministic validator. Declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses) as recorded in execution/model_configuration.json (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The recorded model configuration has temperature = null (unset); because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, model outputs may be nondeterministic across independent API sessions—this nondeterminism was anticipated in the preregistration and is relevant when choosing sampling semantics. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied a full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a normalized_configuration plus a boolean valid flag and per-episode diagnostics (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes). Scoring and analysis procedures. Primary outcome: deterministic verifier pass (binary). Primary test: exact two-sided McNemar on paired contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00). Confidence intervals: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness treatment: primary analysis uses complete_pair_primary (exclude incomplete pairs); preregistered sensitivity treats failed guarded outputs as failures but was not invoked because no failures occurred. Execution accounting and contamination controls. The adapter enforced session isolation and performed contamination checks (session-hash verification, duplicate-response flags); unit-tests for parser/mapping transformations were run and passed prior to batch execution. Runtime audits recorded completed_episode_count = 300, complete_pair_count =150, model_calls_used = 151, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0, and cache_miss_count = 151. All logs, provider traces, and verifier traces were archived and form the basis for the artifact-grounded analysis.
sections.results: Execution and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider accounting and stage counts were recorded: model_calls_used = 151; shared_initial_generation = 150; repair-stage invocations = 1; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; contamination_summary.csv recorded zero flags. Primary numeric outcomes. Paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline): n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv). Repair diagnostics. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150) and converted a single initially invalid candidate to valid under the deterministic verifier; median guarded revision iterations = 0 (IQR = 0). Representative example. Task-000001 (seed=1) intent: migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600 with a shutdown/configure/restore sequence. Shared-initial and both condition responses matched the preregistered reference four-command sequence; validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. Sensitivity and missingness. No failed or unscorable episodes occurred; preregistered sensitivity analyses treating missing guarded outputs as failures were not invoked. Interpretation. Under the executed estimand (C vs A with shared_initial_candidate and a one-repair budget) the guarded pipeline produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. The observed baseline success rate (≈99.33%) invalidated the preregistered power assumption (target detectable effect = +15 pp) and produced a ceiling effect: with n_11 = 149 and only one discordant pair, the paired analysis contains minimal discordant information to detect moderate absolute improvements.
sections.discussion: Ceiling effect and methodological implications. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline competence; the observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 left almost no headroom for a +15 pp detectable improvement. Practically, this implies that confirmatory NetOps trials should incorporate a brief baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks) sampled from the planned generator and prompt design to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant-pair proportions before fixing N. Sampling semantics and estimand interpretation. The shared_initial_candidate semantics used here isolate the marginal value of a repair applied to an identical initial sampled candidate; alternative semantics (independent per-condition sampling, multiple initial draws, or larger repair budgets) estimate different operational questions and typically require different power planning because they change expected discordant-pair proportions and model-call budgets. Cost–benefit and repair budgets. Provider accounting shows the operational cost of the enforced one-repair budget: model_calls_used = 151 for 150 intents and only one repair invoked. When baseline competence is high, per-conversion marginal cost is large; when baseline competence is lower, repairs can convert many failures but exhibit diminishing returns as repair counts increase. Construct and external validity. Construct validity depends on mapping correctness from textual LLM outputs to verifier inputs and on verifier coverage; unit-tests passed and no parse failures occurred, but verifier-coverage remains a source of residual uncertainty. External validity is limited by a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic small-topology tasks (4–32 nodes); results do not generalize to larger, heterogeneous production networks or other models. Operational affordances beyond pass/fail. Deterministic guarded workflows produce machine-actionable artifacts (normalized_configuration, violation_codes) that improve auditability and triage even when pass/fail differences are small. Threats and residual risks. We did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; prior work documents claim-to-action vulnerabilities, so separate adversary-driven evaluations are required to assess security properties of agentic NetOps workflows.
sections.conclusion: We conducted a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting versus constrained prompting plus one verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 the guarded pipeline increased verifier passes from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically trivial and statistically non-significant effect (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.02]). The primary scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include a short baseline-calibration pilot to avoid ceiling effects and preserve inferential power. Practically, researchers and practitioners should (a) explicitly declare generation semantics and repair budgets when reporting effects, (b) include provider-call accounting in cost–benefit planning, and (c) run pilot baseline checks prior to confirmatory sampling. The archived execution and analysis artifacts support reproducible follow-up experiments that vary sampling semantics, repair budgets, model families, and topology scale.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only the declared model gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or model sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Execution semantics: shared_initial_candidate semantics and the adapter-enforced one-repair budget mean this run measures the marginal effect of repairing a fixed initial candidate; independent per-condition sampling or larger repair budgets would estimate different operational contrasts.

Ceiling effect and power mismatch: observed baseline correctness (149/150) was far higher than preregistered pilot assumptions (detectable +15 pp), reducing inferential power and producing minimal discordant information for the paired test.

Verifier coverage and mapping: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants; measurement depends on correct mapping from textual model outputs to verifier inputs and on verifier expressiveness.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted adversarial studies are necessary to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
